Operations.Name: PoolDatasetLock
Operations.Description:
Locks `id` dataset. It will unmount the dataset and its children before locking.

After the dataset has been unmounted, system will set immutable flag on the dataset's mountpoint where

is unlocked, it will not be affected by this change and consumers can continue consuming it.

Arguments.Description: Options for locking the dataset, such as force unmount settings.

Operations.Name: PoolDatasetQuery
Operations.Description:
Query Pool Datasets with `query-filters` and `query-options`.

We provide two ways to retrieve datasets. The first is a flat structure (default), where
all datasets in the system are returned as separate objects which contain all data
there is for their children. This retrieval type is slightly slower because of duplicates in each object.
The second type is hierarchical, where only top level datasets are returned in the list. They contain all the
children in the `children` key. This retrieval type is slightly faster.
These options are controlled by the `query-options.extra.flat` attribute (default true).

In some cases it might be desirable to only retrieve details of a dataset itself and not it's children, in this
case `query-options.extra.retrieve_children` should be explicitly specified and set to `false` which will
result in children not being retrieved.

In case only some properties are desired to be retrieved for datasets, consumer should specify
`query-options.extra.properties` which when `null` ( which is the default ) will retrieve all properties
and otherwise a list can be specified like `["type", "used", "available"]` to retrieve selective properties.
If no properties are desired, in that case an empty list should be sent. It should be noted that specifying
empty list will still retrieve user properties. If user properties are not desired, in that case
`query-options.extra.retrieve_user_props` should be set to `false`.

`query-options.extra.snapshots` can be set to retrieve snapshot(s) of dataset in question.

`query-options.extra.snapshots_recursive` can be set to retrieve snapshot(s) recursively of dataset in question.
If `query-options.extra.snapshots_recursive` and `query-options.extra.snapshots` are set, snapshot(s) will be
retrieved recursively.

`query-options.extra.snapshots_properties` can be specified to list out properties which should be retrieved
for snapshot(s) related to each dataset. By default only name of the snapshot would be retrieved, however
if `null` is specified all properties of the snapshot would be retrieved in this case.

Arguments.Name: filters
Arguments.Description: List of filters for query results. See API documentation for "Query Methods" for more guidance.

Arguments.Name: options
Arguments.Description: Query options including pagination, ordering, and additional parameters.

Rename a pool dataset `id`.

No safety checks are performed when renaming ZFS resources. If the dataset is in use by services such

Proceed only if you are certain the ZFS resource is not in use and fully understand the risks.
Set Force to continue.

Arguments.Name: data
Arguments.Description: The rename operation options including the new name and safety flags.

Operations.Name: PoolDatasetUnlock
Operations.Description:
Unlock dataset `id` (and its children if `unlock_options.recursive` is `true`).

If `id` dataset is not encrypted an exception will be raised. There is one exception:
when `id` is a root dataset and `unlock_options.recursive` is specified, encryption
validation will not be performed for `id`. This allow unlocking encrypted children for the entire pool `id`.

There are two ways to supply the key(s)/passphrase(s) for unlocking a dataset:

1. Upload a json file which contains encrypted dataset keys (it will be read from the input pipe if
`unlock_options.key_file` is `true`). The format is the one that is used for exporting encrypted dataset keys
(`pool.export_keys`).

2. Specify a key or a passphrase for each unlocked dataset using `unlock_options.datasets`.

Arguments.Name: id
Arguments.Description: The dataset ID (full path) to unlock.

Arguments.Name: options
Arguments.Description: Options for unlocking including force settings, recursion, and dataset-specific keys.

Operations.Description: Updates a dataset/zvol `id`.

Models.Name: PoolDatasetEncryptionSummary
Models.Description:
There are 2 keys which show if a recursive unlock operation is done for `id`, which dataset will be unlocked and     if not why it won't be unlocked. The keys namely are `unlock_successful` and `unlock_error`. The former is a     boolean value showing if unlock would succeed/fail. The latter is description why it failed if it failed.

In some cases it's possible that the provided key/passphrase is valid but the path where the dataset is supposed     to be mounted after being unlocked already exists and is not empty. In this case, unlock operation would fail and     `unlock_error` will reflect this error appropriately. This can be overridden by setting     `options.datasets.X.force` boolean flag or by setting `options.force` flag. In practice, when the dataset is     going to be unlocked and these flags have been provided to `pool.dataset.unlock`, system will rename the     directory/file path where the dataset should be mounted resulting in successful unlock of the dataset.

If a dataset is already unlocked, it will show up as true for "unlock_successful" regardless of what key user     provided as the unlock keys in the output are to reflect what a real unlock operation would behave. If user is     interested in seeing if a provided key is valid or not, then the key to look out for in the output is "valid_key"     which based on what system has in database or if a user provided one, validates the key and sets a boolean value     for the dataset.

Fields.Name: KeyFormat
Fields.Description: The format of the encryption key (hex, raw, or passphrase).

Fields.Name: KeyPresentInDatabase
Fields.Description: Whether an encryption key for this dataset exists in the system database.

Fields.Name: Locked
Fields.Description: Whether the dataset is currently locked.

Fields.Name: Name
Fields.Description: The dataset name.

Fields.Name: UnlockError
Fields.Description: Error message if unlock would fail, or `null` if unlock would succeed.

Fields.Name: UnlockSuccessful
Fields.Description: Whether an unlock operation would be successful.

Fields.Name: ValidKey
Fields.Description: Whether the provided key is valid for this dataset.

Fields.Description: The raw string value of the ZFS property as stored in the pool. Can be null if not set.

Fields.Name: Source
Fields.Description: Indicates where the property value originates from.

Fields.Name: SourceInfo
Fields.Description: Additional metadata about the property source, such as the parent dataset for inherited values.

Fields.Name: Value
Fields.Description: The current effective value of the ZFS property as a string. Can be null if inherited or not set.

Models.Name: PoolDatasetRenameData
Models.Description: The rename operation options including the new name and safety flags.

Fields.Name: Force
Fields.Description:
This operation does not check whether the dataset is currently in use. Renaming an active dataset may disrupt     SMB shares, iSCSI targets, snapshots, replication, and other services.

Set Force only if you understand and accept the risks.

Fields.Name: NewName
Fields.Description: The new name for the dataset.

Fields.Name: Recursive
Fields.Description: Whether to recursively rename child datasets.

Fields.Name: Id
Fields.Description: The UID, GID, or name to which the quota applies. If `quota_type` is 'DATASET', then `id` must be either     `QUOTA` or `REFQUOTA`.

Fields.Name: QuotaType
Fields.Description:
The type of quota to apply to the dataset. There are three over-arching types of quotas for ZFS datasets:

* **Dataset quotas and refquotas.** If a `DATASET` quota type is specified in this API call, then the API acts as     a wrapper for `pool.dataset.update`.
* **User and group quotas.** These limit the amount of disk space consumed by files that are owned by the     specified users or groups. If the respective "object quota" type is specfied, then the quota limits the number     of objects that may be owned by the specified user or group.
* **Project quotas.** These limit the amount of disk space consumed by files that are owned by the specified     project. *Project quotas are not yet implemented.*

Fields.Name: QuotaValue
Fields.Description: The quota size in bytes. Setting a value of `0` removes the user or group quota.

Models.Name: PoolDatasetUnlockAnswer
Models.Description: Results of the unlock operation including successful and failed datasets.

Fields.Name: Failed
Fields.Description: Object containing datasets that failed to unlock and their respective error messages.

Fields.Name: Unlocked
Fields.Description: Array of dataset names that were successfully unlocked.

Models.Name: PoolDatasetUnlockOptions
Models.Description: Options for unlocking including force settings, recursion, and dataset-specific keys.

Fields.Name: Datasets
Fields.Description: List of specific datasets with their individual unlock options.

Fields.Name: Force
Fields.Description: In some cases it's possible that the provided key/passphrase is valid but the path where the dataset is     supposed to be mounted after being unlocked already exists and is not empty. In this case, unlock operation would     fail. This can be overridden by setting `datasets.X.force` boolean flag or by setting `force` flag. When any of     these flags are set, system will rename the existing directory/file path where the dataset should be mounted     resulting in successful unlock of the dataset.

Fields.Name: KeyFile
Fields.Description: Whether to use a key file instead of a passphrase for unlocking encrypted datasets.

Fields.Name: Recursive
Fields.Description: Whether to recursively unlock child datasets.

Fields.Name: ToggleAttachments
Fields.Description: Whether attachments should be put in action after unlocking the dataset(s). Toggling attachments can     theoretically lead to service interruption when daemons configurations are reloaded (this should not happen, and     if this happens it should be considered a bug). As TrueNAS does not have a state for resources that should be     unlocked but are still locked, disabling this option will put the system into an inconsistent state so it should     really never be disabled.

Fields.Name: Force
Fields.Description: Force unlock even if the mount path already exists and is not empty.

Fields.Name: Key
Fields.Description: Raw hex-encoded encryption key for this dataset.

Fields.Name: Name
Fields.Description: The dataset name to unlock.

Fields.Name: Passphrase
Fields.Description: Passphrase for this dataset if using passphrase-based encryption.

Fields.Name: Recursive
Fields.Description: Apply the key or passphrase to all encrypted children.

Models.Name: PoolDatasetUpdateData
Models.Description: The dataset properties to update.

Fields.Name: Aclmode
Fields.Description: How Access Control Lists are handled when chmod is used.

Fields.Name: Acltype
Fields.Description: The type of Access Control List system to use.

Fields.Name: Atime
Fields.Description: Whether file access times are updated when files are accessed.

Fields.Name: Checksum
Fields.Description: Checksum algorithm to verify data integrity. Higher security algorithms like SHA256 provide better     protection but use more CPU.

Fields.Name: Comments
Fields.Description: Comments or description for the dataset.

Fields.Name: Compression
Fields.Description: Compression algorithm to use for the dataset. Higher numbered variants provide better compression     but use more CPU. 'INHERIT' uses the parent dataset's setting.

Fields.Name: Copies
Fields.Description: Number of copies of data blocks to maintain for redundancy.

Fields.Name: CreateAncestors
Fields.Description: Whether to create any missing parent datasets.

Fields.Name: Deduplication
Fields.Description: Deduplication setting. 'ON' enables dedup, 'VERIFY' enables with checksum verification, 'OFF' disables.

Fields.Name: Exec
Fields.Description: Whether files in this dataset can be executed.

Fields.Name: ForceSize
Fields.Description: Force creation even if the size is not optimal.

Fields.Name: Managedby
Fields.Description: Identifies which service or system manages this dataset.

Fields.Name: Quota
Fields.Description: Maximum disk space this dataset and its children can consume in bytes.

Fields.Name: QuotaCritical
Fields.Description: Percentage of dataset quota at which to issue a critical alert. 0-100 or 'INHERIT'.

Fields.Name: QuotaWarning
Fields.Description: Percentage of dataset quota at which to issue a warning. 0-100 or 'INHERIT'.

Fields.Name: Readonly
Fields.Description: Whether the dataset is read-only.

Fields.Name: Recordsize
Fields.Description: The suggested block size for files in this filesystem dataset.

Fields.Name: Refquota
Fields.Description: Maximum disk space this dataset itself can consume in bytes.

Fields.Name: RefquotaCritical
Fields.Description: Percentage of reference quota at which to issue a critical alert. 0-100 or 'INHERIT'.

Fields.Name: RefquotaWarning
Fields.Description: Percentage of reference quota at which to issue a warning. 0-100 or 'INHERIT'.

Fields.Name: Refreservation
Fields.Description: Minimum disk space guaranteed to this dataset itself in bytes.

Fields.Name: Reservation
Fields.Description: Minimum disk space guaranteed to this dataset and its children in bytes.

Fields.Name: Snapdev
Fields.Description: Controls visibility of volume snapshots under /dev/zvol/.

Fields.Name: Snapdir
Fields.Description: Controls visibility of the `.zfs/snapshot` directory. 'DISABLED' hides snapshots, 'VISIBLE' shows them,     'HIDDEN' makes them accessible but not listed.

Fields.Name: SpecialSmallBlockSize
Fields.Description: Size threshold below which blocks are stored on special vdevs.

Fields.Name: Sync
Fields.Description: Synchronous write behavior for the dataset.

Fields.Name: UserProperties
Fields.Description: Custom user-defined properties to set on the dataset.

Fields.Name: UserPropertiesUpdate
Fields.Description: Array of user property updates to apply to the dataset.

Fields.Name: Volsize
Fields.Description: The volume size in bytes; supposed to be a multiple of the block size.

Fields.Name: Key
Fields.Description: User property key in namespace:property format.

Fields.Name: Remove
Fields.Description: Whether to remove this user property from the dataset.

Fields.Name: Value
Fields.Description: New value for the user property. Not required if removing the property.
